ministryWordsPage.mainHeading: The Acting Minister of Interior, Major General Emad Mustafa Al-Trabelsi, participated today, Monday, in the 41st session of the Council of Arab Interior Ministers in Tunisia.
ministryWordsPage.paragraph: The Acting Minister of Interior, Major General Emad Mustafa Al-Trabelsi, participated today, Monday, in the 41st session of the Council of Arab Interior Ministers in Tunisia, in the presence of interior ministers of Arab countries, high-level security delegations, as well as representatives from the League of Arab States, the International Criminal Police Organization 'Interpol,' the United Nations Office on Counter-Terrorism, the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime, Naif Arab University for Security Sciences, and the Arab Police Sports Federation. Among the key topics discussed during the session were the preparation of the 11th Arab Security Plan, the 9th Arab Media Plan for Security Awareness and Crime Prevention, and the 8th Interim Plan for the Arab Road Safety Strategy.

decisionDetailsPage.breadcrumb: Home - About the Ministry - Decisions - The Minister of Interior decides to merge several security directorates affiliated with the Libyan government
decisionDetailsPage.mainHeading: The Minister of Interior decides to merge several security directorates affiliated with the Libyan government
decisionDetailsPage.paragraph: The Minister of Interior, Major General Essam Abu Zariba, issued separate decisions to merge several security directorates affiliated with the Libyan government in the eastern, southeastern, and southwestern regions, reducing their number from 37 directorates to 16. According to the distribution of the directorates, the Benghazi Security Directorate includes (Benghazi, Suluq, Qaminis, Tokra, and Al-Abya), the Butnan Directorate includes (Tobruk, Umm Sa'ad, and Bir Al-Ashhab), the Derna Security Directorate includes (Derna and Umm Al-Razam), the Quba Security Directorate includes (Quba, Al-Abrak, and Al-Qayqab), the Green Mountain Directorate includes (Shahat, Al-Bayda, Werdama, and part of the Coast Directorate), the Marj Directorate includes (Marj, Jardas Al-Abid, and part of the Coast Directorate), the Ajdabiya Directorate includes (Ajdabiya, Ras Lanuf, and the area up to Bishr Police Center), and so on. These measures aim to enhance security and public safety.

emergency_cases.title: Handling Emergency Cases
emergency_cases.breadcrumb: Home - About Ministry - Handling Emergency Cases
emergency_cases.important_numbers_description: In case of emergency, you can contact the following numbers from anywhere in Libya
emergency_cases.traffic_accidents_description: In case of an accident, call the police at the free emergency number 999 from anywhere in Libya and report the accident location and any injuries requiring an ambulance. Follow police instructions and remember that all accidents must be reported, no matter how minor. For minor traffic accidents, move your car to the side of the road if possible to avoid obstructing traffic.

fire_instructions.0: Call the free emergency number (997) from anywhere in Libya and follow the instructions.
fire_instructions.1: Evacuate the area immediately and head to the nearest emergency exit.
fire_instructions.2: Move toward the exits calmly and do not rush.
fire_instructions.3: Do not stay to collect your belongings under any circumstances.
fire_instructions.4: If possible, close doors as you leave to prevent the fire from spreading.
fire_instructions.5: Do not use the elevator when leaving.
fire_instructions.6: If possible, try to extinguish the fire with available extinguishers without risking your life or others'.
fire_instructions.7: Do not return to the building until the police or civil defense declares it safe.
fire_instructions.8: Utilize smart protection and control systems, if available, to detect and prevent fires in commercial buildings and residential apartments.

overview.ministry_name: Ministry of Interior, Government of Libya
overview.ministry_description: The Ministry of Interior of the Libyan government implements the legislations, laws, regulations, and decisions necessary to ensure the country's security, protect lives, honor, and property, and execute the policies, plans, and programs required for enforcing the legislations in the field of security and policing.
overview.task_1: 1 – Monitoring the implementation of the ministry's plans and policies and working to enhance security performance levels.
overview.task_2: 2 – Participating in preparing financial estimates necessary for drafting the ministry's budget projects.
overview.task_3: 3 – Maintaining security by taking the necessary measures and procedures to ensure its achievement.
overview.task_4: 4 – Preparing studies and research on security and devising plans to ensure its achievement.
overview.task_5: 5 – Taking actions related to expenditures from the ministry's budget in accordance with the applicable legislation.
overview.task_6: 6 – Contracting for the implementation of projects specific to the ministry in accordance with the applicable legislation.
overview.task_7: 7 – Preparing necessary plans and programs to prevent and address crimes and safeguard lives, honor, and property.
overview.task_8: 8 – Handling personal status matters, protecting and securing tourists, tourist sites, and heritage sites, and guarding facilities, establishments, and critical objectives in accordance with applicable legislation.
overview.task_9: 9 – Recruiting, training, and preparing qualified technical personnel to work in the police and training members of public security.
overview.task_10: 10 – Conducting investigations, collecting evidence, identifying individuals, and examining crime scenes using scientific and technical methods to collect and preserve material evidence.
overview.task_11: 11 – Developing and implementing civil defense plans and projects, combating fires, addressing general and natural disasters, training individuals on civil defense tasks, and forming air raid and fire monitoring teams.
overview.task_12: 12 – Conducting minefield surveys, detecting and clearing bombs, and collecting, transporting, and disposing of explosives.
overview.task_13: 13 – Carrying out land and sea rescue operations.
overview.task_14: 14 – Handling traffic affairs on public roads, police aviation, road patrols (vehicular and pedestrian), and ensuring wired and wireless communication and operations room management.
overview.task_15: 15 – Raising security awareness among citizens to address fires, natural disasters, and crime prevention through security media and issuing related publications.
overview.task_16: 16 – Managing passports, nationality, ID cards, civil status matters, foreign residency, and immigration, and monitoring entry and exit movements through designated ports.
overview.task_17: 17 – Handling public relations and international cooperation within the ministry's domain.
overview.task_18: 18 – Managing Arab and international police affairs.
overview.task_19: 19 – Supervising entities affiliated with the ministry.
overview.task_20: 20 – Taking necessary measures to appoint officials for entities affiliated with the ministry in accordance with applicable legislation.
overview.task_21: 21 – Issuing decisions on appointments, promotions, transfers, deputations, and loans in accordance with the ministry's budget and applicable legislation.
overview.task_23: 23 – Proposing programs and plans to improve the efficiency and performance level of ministry employees in coordination with relevant entities.
overview.task_24: 24 – Exercising the competencies prescribed by applicable legislation.

faq.item1.question: The applicant submitted a request for a visitor's permit but has not yet received approval.

faq.item2.question: Can the criminal record certificate be amended after issuance?

faq.item3.question: What are the required documents for a work permit?
faq.item3.answer: The required documents include: a copy of the passport, a personal photo, an employment contract, and any additional documents requested by the relevant authority.
faq.item4.question: How can I update my residence information?
faq.item4.answer: To update your residence information, please visit the website of the Federal Authority for Identity and Citizenship or their smart app.
faq.item5.question: Can I apply for a multiple-entry visit visa?
faq.item5.answer: Yes, you can apply for a multiple-entry visit visa through the website of the Federal Authority for Identity and Citizenship.

meetingsDetails.title: Meetings
meetingsDetails.mainTitle: Minister of Interior Inspects Security Conditions in Murzuq Municipality
meetingsDetails.description: The Minister of Interior, Major General Essam Abu Zariba, conducted an inspection visit to the Municipality of Murzuq today, Wednesday, accompanied by the Head of the Ministry's Office in the Southern Region, the Head of the Criminal Investigation Authority, the Director of the General Directorate of Security Operations, and the Director of the General Directorate of Central Support. He was received by the Director of Security, Major General Dr. Osama Awidan, along with several security leaders, the Mayor of the Municipality, and the city's dignitaries and elders. As part of his field tour to monitor security conditions and enhance stability, the Minister held an extensive meeting with the Municipal Council, dignitaries, and elders of the city at the Security Directorate headquarters. During the meeting, he listened to their security demands and needs and discussed the challenges facing the municipality in this context. The attendees commended the Minister's continuous efforts, expressing their appreciation for his personal commitment to improving the security situation through his repeated visits to the region and his direct follow-up on security developments there. For his part, the Minister emphasized the importance of close cooperation between the Ministry of Interior and the local community, affirming that the Ministry will spare no effort in enhancing security and stability, pursuing lawbreakers, and protecting citizens. He also praised the role of the city's elders and dignitaries in supporting the Security Directorate and police stations and their solidarity with security personnel in their efforts to enforce the law and restore stability. The Minister reiterated that the Ministry places the security of citizens and the safety of Libya at the top of its priorities and is committed to taking the necessary measures to enhance security across all parts of the country.

minister_security_meeting: The Minister of Interior holds an extensive security meeting at the Al-Shati Security Directorate
minister_name: Minister of Interior, Major General Essam Abu Zreiba
meeting_details: The Minister of Interior, Major General Essam Abu Zariba, held an expanded meeting with security leaders at the Security Directorate of Al-Shate, today, Thursday, in the presence of the Head of the Criminal Investigation Authority, Major General Ahmed Al-Shamikh, the Head of the Anti-Illegal Immigration Authority, Major General Salah Al-Khafifi, the Director of Security, Major General Wahbi Al-Rakh, and the directors of the branches and security departments, in addition to the heads of the centers and departments affiliated with the directorate. During the meeting, the Minister emphasized the importance of strict adherence to the implementation of the law without leniency, stressing that citizens place their hopes in the security agencies to achieve security and stability, and that there is no room for leniency with any threats to public peace. The Minister also addressed the issue of appointments within the security institution, pointing out the necessity of establishing clear criteria to ensure the competence of security personnel and their ability to bear the responsibilities entrusted to them. The meeting discussed the main security challenges facing the region, and ways to improve security performance through developing emergency plans, enhancing coordination between various agencies, and providing the necessary supplies to the directorate and its components. The Minister issued instructions to quickly provide the directorate with the resources it needs, in accordance with what was presented by the Director of Security in Al-Shate.
